facts: The comment on the paper was made by Allen H. Boozer.
The paper discussed is titled "A Simple Model of Current Ramp-Up and Ramp-Down in Tokamaks."
The comment was dated August 25, 2026.
The focus of the comment is on improving efficiency and stability in plasma operations.
The paper "Nuclear Fusion66, 016012 (2026)" was authored by Richard Fitzpatrick.
The paper critiques errors in the understanding of poloidal magnetic flux evolution in tokamaks.
Fitzpatrick presents a new expression for loop voltage in the paper.
The journal Nuclear Fusion prohibits the mention of "private communication" in responses.
Richard Fitzpatrick's Nuclear Fusion paper was accepted on October 14, 2025.
The Nuclear Fusion paper was published online on November 6, 2025.
Fitzpatrick's paper contains misunderstandings of Faraday’s Law in toroidal plasmas.
The Nuclear Fusion journal's policy prevents the publication of comments that disclose private communications.
Richard Fitzpatrick's 2026 Nuclear Fusion paper has been criticized for misunderstanding Faraday's Law.
The paper fails to recognize the significance of the toroidal flux and its relationship to the poloidal flux.
Key errors in the paper include neglecting the influence of the central solenoid's flux.
The analysis of the paper is complicated by a lack of consideration for the time-dependent nature of poloidal flux.
The author addresses misquoting issues in a Nuclear Fusion article.
The Nuclear Fusion policy allows for false claims to be supported by private communications.
A specific misquote in the abstract of the Nuclear Fusion paper oversimplified the author's views on ramp-down times.
The author emphasizes the need for improved understanding and diagnostics of plasma behavior in tokamak power plants.

Appendix A derives a new expression for loop voltage for toroidal plasmas. The electric field parallel to the magnetic field incorporates bootstrap and direct current drive current densities. The Pfirsch-Schlüter current density balances the divergence of the perpendicular current density. The net plasma current density is defined to be divergence-free.
